transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I'm having some trouble with my eating habits. It usually happens at night after everyone goes to bed. I’ll tell myself I’m just going to have some leftovers, and then... I don't know, I just keep going. I'll suddenly realize I’ve eaten half a tray of catered pasta from work, the dessert from a client dinner, and whatever snacks were left in the pantry, all in one sitting. It's just become a real problem.
After one of these episodes, do you ever try to get rid of the food or make up for it—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot?

No, I don't do any of those things. I've never tried to make myself throw up, and I don't take laxatives. I... I don't really fast or do any crazy workouts the next day, either. I mostly just wake up feeling really uncomfortably full and upset with myself, but I don't do anything to actually get rid of the food.
How often would you say these binge eating episodes happen—for example, how many times per week over the past few months?

For the last three months or so, I'd say it happens at least one night almost every week. Usually it's after a late work event, or maybe if I've had an argument with someone. And... well, some weeks it happens twice.
During these episodes, do you find yourself eating in secret or avoiding others because you feel embarrassed about how much you're eating?

Well, I'm not really sure if I'm actively hiding. Like I mentioned, it almost always happens late at night when my family is already asleep. 

I guess... I mean, I definitely wouldn't want my husband or anyone else to walk into the kitchen and see me eating like that. It would be really embarrassing. So I do make sure I'm alone, but I just haven't really thought about it as doing it in secret until you said that.
During these episodes, would you say you're eating much faster than you normally would, like wolfing the food down quickly?

Yes, definitely. I eat really fast during those times. Usually, I'm just standing at the kitchen island, maybe scrolling through some work emails on my phone, and I'm eating so quickly that I barely even taste the food. 

Sometimes I just... I look down and the containers are already empty before I've really even registered what I was eating. It happens very fast.
How much distress or upset do these binge eating episodes cause you afterward?

It causes quite a bit of distress, honestly. Afterward, I just feel... really embarrassed and disgusted with myself. I try to be a very disciplined person, and it feels like I’ve completely blown that whole image when I do this. I'll usually just sit there feeling awful, thinking about how I really should have gone for a run or done some yoga instead of eating all that.
